BiblicalUsage: Karkom is the crocus — saffron, named among the spices of the garden: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the garden's spices are the language of love: the bride's garden is fragrant with the best of things, and love itself is the chief spice.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
